# 42 U.S.C. § 426: Hospital Insurance Entitlement

## Subsection (a) - Age 65 Requirement

The statute establishes that individuals aged 65 and older become eligible for hospital insurance benefits. Specifically, it states: "Every individual who—(1) has attained age 65, and (2)..." must meet additional criteria regarding Social Security benefits or railroad retirement status to qualify.

The individual must either be entitled to monthly insurance benefits under Social Security, be a qualified railroad retirement beneficiary, or meet certain government employment requirements.

## Subsection (b) - Disability 24-Month Requirement

For individuals under age 65, the law requires a longer waiting period. The provision specifies: "Every individual who—(1) has not attained age 65, and (2)...is entitled to, and has for 24 calendar months been entitled to..." disability insurance benefits or certain survivor benefits.

The entitlement begins "with the later of (I) July 1973 or (II) the twenty-fifth month of his entitlement" to qualifying disability benefits, demonstrating the 24-month prerequisite before hospital insurance coverage commences for disabled beneficiaries under age 65.

Based on the search results, here's what I found about Medicare eligibility for people under 65 receiving disability benefits:

## Automatic Medicare Enrollment After 24 Months

People under 65 are eligible for Medicare if they've gotten Social Security Disability Insurance (SSDI) or certain Railroad Retirement Board (RRB) disability benefits for at least 24 months.

If you're under 65 and getting disability benefits from Social Security, you get Medicare automatically after getting disability benefits for 24 months or when you turn 65 – whichever comes first.

## Automatic Enrollment Process

People living in the U.S. and U.S. Territories (except Puerto Rico) who are already getting Social Security—either because of disability or retirement—are automatically signed up for Part A and Part B when they're first eligible. They get a packet of information a few months before they turn 65 or when they get their 25th month of Social Security Disability or Railroad Retirement Board (RRB) benefits.

## Special Exceptions

There are two conditions that don't require the 24-month wait: If you're getting Social Security disability benefits, you'll get Medicare automatically after getting disability benefits for 24 months. If you have ALS (also called Lou Gehrig's disease) you'll get Medicare automatically as soon as you start getting disability benefits. For End-Stage Renal Disease (ESRD), Medicare typically begins three months after dialysis starts or the month of a successful kidney transplant.
